LawProactive connects injured Bishop workers with an independent attorney who can sort out workers' comp from a possible third-party claim, at no cost to you.

about.title: Bishop Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Bishop's economy runs on ranching, tourism, small industry, and the highways that connect them, including US-395 and N Main Street corridors that see steady equipment and delivery traffic. When someone gets hurt working near these roads or on a job site elsewhere in town, most people assume workers' compensation is the only path forward. That's often true against your own employer, but it isn't the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, California law allows a separate claim against that third party, on top of any workers' comp benefits. With Bishop's population under 4,000, local job sites, delivery routes, and highway work often overlap in ways that create these third-party situations. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in Inyo County who can look at your specific injury and explain your options plainly.

whyChoose.title: Why Bishop Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Sort Out Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' compensation usually blocks a lawsuit against your employer, but it doesn't shield a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker. An attorney can review your incident to see if a separate claim applies.

items.title: We Know the 30-Day Reporting Window Matters
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report an on-the-job injury to their employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your benefits, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Are on Your Side
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your protections before you decide anything.

items.question: I was hurt while driving for work near N Main Street. Do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: Possibly both. Workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against them. An independent attorney can look at the details and explain which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: What's the deadline if a third party caused my workplace injury in Bishop?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. Workers' comp reporting deadlines are separate and much shorter, so it's worth understanding both timelines rather than assuming one covers everything.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No, retaliation against an employee for reporting a work injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal under California law. If you're facing pressure or pushback after an injury near a job site in Inyo County, it's worth talking with an independent attorney about your options.
